newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The bourse's surge upwards yesterday surprised even brokers, setting yet another record with the general price index closing at 1,453.6 points and turnover of 45.2 billion drachmas. Brokers are speaking of an injection of fresh capital from private investors that can total up to 500 million drachmas daily: however, everybody now expects a correction in the next few days.
--The Bank of Greece soaked 200 billion drachmas of 14-day depo funds at interest rates of between 11.85-11.92 percent for the third consecutive week yesterday.
--The National Housing Bank is preparing to expand its portfolio and install new computer systems to avert credit risks, as well as collaborating with US experts in housing finance, Fannie Mae.
--The buying frenzy on the bourse yesterday prompted the president of the Capital Market Commission to warn investors against speculation and to avoid rumopur-based investment decisions.
--Interest rates are forecast to fall below 10.0 percent by the end of March, given the consensus that inflation in February will fall to 6.5 percent and 6.3 percent in March.
--A new bill on the inclusion of property in urban planning grids was submitted to Parliament yesterday by Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis.
--The European Commission yesterday extended aid conditions for the Greek shipping industry until the end of the year, giving the industry some breathing space.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis finally met members of the Thessaly Farmers Coordinating Committee yesterday but there appeared to be no points of reference between the two sides.
--The Hellenic Investment Centre will begin a campaign abroad to appraise foreign investors of investment opportunities, president Nikos Skoulas said yesterday.

--The retail trade created the greatest numbers of new jobs in the period 1991-95, according to a recent survey. Unemployment however continues to rise. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
